newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAfrica labour union welcomes budget tax decisions.
newsitem.headline: SAfrica labour union welcomes budget tax decisions.

text.p: The Federation of South African Labour Unions on Wednesday welcomed decisions in the country's budget not to raise VAT and to provide tax relief to middle income earners.
However, the union grouping representing more than 300,000 skilled members from 20 unions, expressed concern about the new tax implications for dividend income from unit trusts.
"Government must...realise that it is bad policy to increase taxes on savings," Fedsal said in a statement reacting to the release of the 1997/98 budget.
The union cautioned against the equalisation of tax-free lump sum benefits for private and public sector employees without proper consideration of the overall renumeration of public servants.
"Insult will be added to injury by also taxing retirement benefits which were previously tax free for public employees," it said.

Fedsal hailed the government's commitment to social spending but said it feared that the job creation targets of its macroeconomic plan, a five-year programme that maps out South Africa's economic future, may not be met.
South Africa's largest trade union, the Congress of South African Trade Unions, could not be reached for comment.
